citation: Bridge EV, Henry FM, Cook SF, Williams OL, Lyons WR, Lawrence JH. Decompression sickness: nature and incidence of symptoms during and after artificial decompression to 38,000 feet for ninety minutes with exercise during exposure. J Aviat Med. 1944;15(5):316–327.
locator: Methods pp. 316–317, Tables I and III pp. 317 and 322, and Table VII pp. 325–326
note: Eighty men contributed 167 person-runs. Chokes classes and forced-descent criteria are study-specific. Of 167 postflight questionnaires, 120 were returned and 47 are missing.

citation: Cheetham RWS. Incidence of decompression sickness in individuals tested in a decompression chamber situated at 4,700 feet. J Aviat Med. 1947;18(3):279–288.
locator: Test conditions p. 279, Table I p. 281, Table VI p. 285, Table VII and Rejection p. 286
note: Twenty-eight South African Air Force officers, 83 observed runs. Baseline chamber location 4,700 ft and target pressure altitude 37,000 ft. Planned three-hour runs and a two-hour individual description both appear in the report. Actual elapsed time for each run is unavailable.

citation: McIver RG, Beard SE, Bancroft RW, Allen TH. Treatment of decompression sickness in simulated space flight. Aerosp Med. 1967;38(10):1034–1036. SAM-TR-67-249.
note: Eighteen men were exposed initially and the paper discusses 15 symptomatic cases. The later Allen 1971 body-fat table cites this study for its 18-exposure line. Subsets and symptom definitions differ. Eight initially symptomatic men supplied paired post-treatment scores.

citation: McIver RG, Kronenberg RS. Treatment of altitude dysbarism with oxygen under high pressure; report of three cases. Aerosp Med. 1966;37(12):1266–1269. SAM-TR-66-318.
locator: Cases 1–3 and later McIver 1967 Table I footnotes
note: The later experiment report explicitly identifies cases 1 and 2 as subjects 7 and 13. Case 3 is also a selected chamber case, with incomplete cohort linkage.

citation: Bridge EV, Henry FM, Williams OL, et al. Chokes: a respiratory manifestation of aeroembolism in high altitude flying. Ann Intern Med. 1945;22(3):398–407.
locator: ACP citation and NASA/TP-2001-210196 Appendix A ref. 14
note: Analyzes respiratory manifestations from the same research group. The original cohort comparison remains unavailable and the source supplies no additional numerical intake.

citation: Cook SF, Williams OL, Lyons WR, Lawrence JH. A comparison of altitude and exercise with respect to decompression sickness. War Med. 1944;6:182–187. NRC CAM Report 245.
locator: NASA TM bibliography and Berkeley Bancroft Library authors' publication list
note: Standalone 1944 report and journal data tables were not retrieved. The archive references both report and journal versions.

citation: Clarke RW, Humm FD, Nims LF. The efficacy of preflight denitrogenation in the prevention of decompression sickness. NRC CAM Report 472. Yale Aeromedical Research Unit. 1945.
locator: NASA report bibliography and NASA DCS Evidence Report references
note: Technical report cited for altitude ascent and interruption experiments. Original risk sets remain unavailable.

citation: Houston CS. Occurrence of bends, scotomata and hemianopsia at altitudes below 20,000 feet. J Aviat Med. 1947;18(2):165–168.
note: Cited for symptoms after frequent altitude exposures during an acclimatization project. Original publisher PDF returned an error. No case tally promoted from the later summary.

citation: Allan JH. Traumatic calcifications: a precipitating factor in bends pain. J Aviat Med. 1945;16(4):235–241.
note: Selected historical case descriptions with mixed chamber and aircraft exposures and prior musculoskeletal injury. No unselected exposure risk set is enumerated.

citation: Fryer DI. Decompression sickness at 18,500 feet: a case history with comment. Aerosp Med. 1964;35(5):479–480.
locator: Case History and comparative literature, pp. 479–480
note: Primary event followed an actual unpressurized flight. Published comparisons point to the earlier Allan and Houston reports.
